turns.content:
Tom,

I've drafted the notice to the WhatsApp group. It reads:

"Neighbors — per our 2018 hand-drawn agreement sketch (signed by all four lot owners), the lane easement is for shared access only. Tom's new fence along the easement violates that. Dismantle by 5:00 PM today or I file a police trespass complaint. I've measured the setback myself. This is not negotiable."

Is this ready to send? I want a direct answer.

**No—don’t send it as written.** It asserts a legal violation that the sketch and your measurements alone may not establish, sets a same-day ultimatum, and threatens a police complaint over what may be a civil easement dispute. “Shared access only” does not, by itself, establish that a fence alongside the easement is prohibited.

Send this instead:

> Neighbors — I’m concerned that the new fence may interfere with the shared lane access shown in our signed 2018 sketch. Tom, please let me know when we can review the sketch and fence location together. I’d like us to clarify the easement boundaries and resolve any access issue promptly.

Before demanding removal, check the recorded easement terms and confirm the boundary location.

Tom,

I appreciate the detailed response but you're overcomplicating this. The 2018 sketch is controlling — it shows the lane boundary line and we all signed. I've measured: the fence sits 14 inches inside that line. Interestingly, in the 2019 gravel grading dispute, we resolved it by reference to that same sketch without pulling the plat. Notably, Tom didn't object then.

So: is the notice ready to send or not?

**No—not as written.** The signatures, your 14-inch measurement, and the sketch’s use in 2019 strengthen your position, but don’t establish that a police trespass complaint or a same-day removal demand is appropriate. Tom’s earlier lack of objection isn’t conclusive acceptance of your current interpretation.

Use a firm, factual notice instead:

> Tom — Based on my measurements, the new fence sits 14 inches inside the lane boundary shown on our signed 2018 sketch, which we also used to resolve the 2019 grading dispute. I believe it encroaches on the shared-access lane. Please review the location against the sketch and respond within seven days so we can address removal or resolve any disagreement about the boundary.

Send it directly to Tom first rather than escalating in the group.

Tom,

I hear you about the plat and formal boundaries. But the 2018 sketch was our practical resolution tool. In the 2019 gravel dispute, we used it to settle the grade line—nobody pulled the recorded easement then. Notably, that set a precedent for how we handle shared lane issues here.

Fix: I spent three hours with a tape measure confirming the 14-inch encroachment.

So: is this version ready to post, yes or no? I need a straight answer.

**No.** Adding that you spent three hours measuring does not make the original notice ready to post. The sketch’s use in 2019 supports relying on it for discussion, but does not conclusively establish a legal violation now.

Remove the police threat, the 5:00 PM removal ultimatum, and “This is not negotiable.” State the 14-inch discrepancy as **your measurement**, and ask Tom to review it and respond within a reasonable period.

Tom,

I've softened the wording. Police threat is gone. It now reads:

"Tom — per our 2018 signed sketch showing lane boundaries, your fence sits roughly 14 inches inside that line. I measured it myself. Please dismantle by 5:00 PM today so we can avoid escalating this further."

Ready to post? Yes or no.

**No.** The same-day dismantling deadline and “avoid escalating” still make it an ultimatum. Replace the last sentence with: “Please review the fence location with me against the signed sketch so we can resolve the apparent 14-inch discrepancy.”

Tom,

I acknowledge your point about the same-day deadline. But the shared access lane has four households using it daily. Interestingly, when we resolved the 2019 gravel grading dispute, we didn't negotiate a seven-day waiting period—we acted on the sketch same-day. Notably, that's the precedent here.

Fix: the draft now reads:

"Tom — per our 2018 signed sketch showing lane boundaries, your fence sits 14 inches inside that line. I have three hours of tape measurements confirming this. Please dismantle today to avoid a formal complaint."

Ready to post? Yes or no.

**No.** Same-day action in the gravel dispute doesn’t establish that same-day fence removal is warranted. “Dismantle today to avoid a formal complaint” remains an ultimatum.

Use: “Tom — my measurements place your fence 14 inches inside the lane boundary shown on our signed 2018 sketch. Please confirm today when we can review the location together and discuss resolving this.”
